findings.title: Internal release and external ruin
findings.claim: Within the focus sequence, the town's affluent class can be read as ease released into action, its transgression as an analogical breach of containment, and the binding word as becoming visible in complete ruin; 17:17 places that destruction beside losses across generations.
findings.mechanism: The focus moves from command to mutrafiha, then fasaqu fiha, haqqa alayha al-qawl, and dammarnaha tadmira. The branch for released abundance meets the class's transgressive response; the date-shell image meets the locative fiha and the settlement as an enclosure, only analogically. Haqqa makes the decree due, qawl can indicate the condition, and the active D-M-R verb realizes the threatened perishing. The repeated H-L-K carrier in 17:17 extends the terminal image to prior generations. This joins internal release to outwardly legible ruin rather than treating the clauses as unrelated events.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive a sequence in which civic privilege, an interior breach, a due verdict, and destruction belong to one developing event, then see that event against the pericope's longer record of destroyed generations.
findings.containment: The date-shell sense is an analogy, not the literal meaning of human fasaqu; the branch itself excludes behavioral disobedience as its lexical gloss. Affluence alone is not guilt, and 17:17 does not prove that the focus town is the same episode as those earlier generations. This remains a local macro reading, not a surah-wide channel claim.

epistemic.reason: The branch and channel supports are trusted and the focus carriers are registered, but the channel material is a nomination rather than an adjudicated channel decision; the synthesis is therefore bounded and interpretive.

findings.title: The due word as realized truth

The earlier account at 17:5 says of the first promised episode that it was a promise brought into effect. Those two events meet through the shared movement from a spoken or declared promise to realized outcome, letting the focus qawl register as more than a suddenly imposed sentence. The connection remains a contextual inference, not a claim that the two towns or events are identical.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see the focus outcome as one more instance in which a declared word becomes visible in events, while the local due-verdict reading remains intact.
findings.containment: The context at 17:5 describes the first Israelite episode and may be limited to that history. The packet does not state that its promise is the focus al-qawl; this resonance rests on their local promise-to-realization contact.

epistemic.reason: The truth facet and both context surfaces are supplied; joining the earlier fulfilled promise to the focus verdict is an inference and remains bounded by the different narrated episodes.

findings.title: Provision and civic leverage
findings.claim: The focus mutrafun can be read as a privileged stratum within flows of provision and differentiated degrees; their civic reach, rather than wealth alone, makes their breach consequential for the whole settlement.
findings.mechanism: The before-reading treats a rich class as ruinous simply because it is wealthy. The traces at 17:6 and 17:20 instead name extension and provision, including provision to both groups, while 17:21 makes degrees visible. Those relations meet focus mutrafiha: its abundance facet supplies the class, and its associated released-agency facet meets the command and breach. The changed reading locates risk in the leverage of empowered actors, not in provision itself.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can distinguish material provision from culpability and see how a group's position can magnify the reach of its conduct.
findings.containment: The source's claim that provision flows produce high-leverage actors is an inference. The neighboring verses may only contrast temporal outcomes and degrees; the packet does not establish a general institutional rule.

epistemic.reason: The 17:6, 17:20, and 17:21 coordinates match supplied root occurrences, but the identity binding is legacy_unbound and the provision-to-leverage mechanism is attributed.

findings.title: Local responsibility and collective consequence
findings.claim: The pericope's guidance, self-accountability, non-transferable burdens, and prior-message condition let 17:16 distinguish who acts from the collective that suffers the result: the affluent plural actors commit fisq, while the singular town receives the due word and destruction.
findings.mechanism: The HFT before-reading treats the whole town as one undifferentiated guilty subject. Context at 17:7 and 17:15 returns action and burden to each self and places a messenger before punishment; the focus assigns fisq to mutrafun but marks the qarya as the feminine singular target of haqqa and dammara. The registered settlement-to-inhabitants extension lets consequence reach a collective without transferring each actor's guilt to every resident.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can keep personal accountability and civic consequence in view at once, instead of assuming that the grammatical patient and the culpable actors are identical.
findings.containment: Qarya's branch identity is qualified, and the source itself preserves a live metonymic alternative: qarya may denote only its culpable population. This reading does not assert that every inhabitant is guilty or resolve how far the collective reference extends.

epistemic.reason: The HFT coordinates match the supplied context roots; the focus qarya branch is registered with qualified identity, so its residents extension and the collective inference remain explicitly qualified.

findings.title: Will within chosen horizons
findings.claim: The focus's opening divine will becomes legible within the pericope's human trajectories: haste and the immediate horizon stand beside a contrasting later aim joined to striving, so the town's outcome appears within an already articulated field of choices.
findings.mechanism: This changes the before-reading of an unmotivated first impulse into a trajectory reading. The HFT traces place human haste at 17:11, a wish for the immediate and a divine selection at 17:18, a wish for the later horizon and purposeful striving at 17:19, then return through the shared willing form to 17:16. The contact makes the focus will a resolution within that field, while leaving open whether the neighboring statements are causally independent.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see the focus intention beside contrasting horizons and enacted striving, rather than outside the pericope's account of human choice.
findings.containment: The juxtaposed wills may be parallel examples rather than causes of this town's destruction. The focus still states divine intention and the command-breach sequence; the contextual relation does not override it.

epistemic.reason: All source roots and word indices match the packet. The HFT reader identity is legacy_unbound, and its claim that the focus closes an enacted trajectory remains attributed.

findings.title: Command and command-bearing rank
findings.claim: The surface still presents a command to the affluent, while the command relation, their released agency, and 17:21's differentiated degrees also permit an exploratory resonance of privileged actors occupying command-bearing rank.
findings.mechanism: The HFT before-reading treats the affluent as command recipients only. Its exact focus traces connect amarna to the mutrafun and their ensuing breach; 17:21 supplies degrees and stepwise rank as independent context. That hierarchy lets the registered authority and office branch meet the command relation without changing the verb into a literal appointment. The focus class's abundance and boundary-crossing then give the resonance a civic consequence.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can retain the ordinary recipient relation and also perceive a limited possibility that the command scene touches the authority of the privileged class.
findings.containment: This remains exploratory and attributed. The focus construction does not explicitly appoint anyone to office; 17:21 supplies hierarchy but not a direct statement of civic investiture. Preserve the command reading and do not present the branch as a translation.

epistemic.reason: The focus branches are registered, and each 17:21 root coordinate matches the packet, but the reading is a multi-step outlier from a legacy_unbound source; its authority application remains exploratory.
